# Beer distribution game

Build the classic beer distribution game. Four companies form a supply chain for one product: a retailer, a wholesaler, a distributor and a factory, each run by an AI agent. Every week, customers buy from the retailer; weekly customer demand is random, a whole number of cases between 0 and 8. Each week every company ships what it can to the company below it, then places an order with the company above it (the factory instead starts production). Orders reach the supplier the following week, and shipments take two weeks to arrive; production also takes two weeks. Everyone starts with 12 cases in stock and 4 cases already on the way on each shipping link. Demand a company cannot fill becomes backlog and must be shipped later. Each company pays $0.50 per case in stock and $1.00 per case of backlog at the end of every week. Companies only see their own stock, backlog, incoming orders and deliveries, never the others' positions. The game lasts 20 weeks and the team's goal is the lowest total cost.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `customer_demand` — a list of the cases customers demanded each week, in week order.
- `factory_orders` — a list of the cases the factory put into production each week, in week order.
- `costs_by_role` — a map from role ("retailer", "wholesaler", "distributor", "factory") to that company's total cost.
- `total_team_cost` — the sum of all four companies' costs.
- `bullwhip_ratio` — the variance of the factory's weekly production orders divided by the variance of weekly customer demand.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

brief.situation: You run one company in a four-stage beer supply chain — a retailer, a wholesaler, a distributor and a factory — each run by an agent. Customers buy beer from the retailer every week. The product is a single brand of beer, measured in cases.
brief.rules: The game lasts {$inputs.weeks} weeks. Each week runs in this order: first every company ships to the company below it (the factory ships nothing downstream), then every company orders from the company above it (the factory starts production instead of ordering). An order reaches the supplier the following week. Shipments take {$inputs.ship_lead} weeks to arrive and production takes {$inputs.prod_lead} weeks to arrive. Demand a company cannot fill becomes backlog and must be shipped later. At the end of every week each company pays {$inputs.holding_cost|money} per case in stock and {$inputs.backlog_cost|money} per case of backlog. Every company starts with {$inputs.start_stock} cases in stock and {$inputs.start_pipeline} cases on the way on each shipping link. You only ever see your own stock, backlog, incoming orders and incoming deliveries — never the other companies' positions. The team's goal is the lowest total cost.

roles.retailer: You are the retailer. Customers buy beer from you every week; you ship to them and you order from the wholesaler.
roles.wholesaler: You are the wholesaler. You ship to the retailer and you order from the distributor.
roles.distributor: You are the distributor. You ship to the wholesaler and you order from the factory.
roles.factory: You are the factory. You ship to the distributor and, instead of ordering, you start production.

stages.brief: Ship beer to the company below you. If you owe backlog, ship at least that much whenever you can.
stages.order: $it.role == retailer and 0 or ($it.role == wholesaler and 1 or ($it.role == distributor and 2 or 3))

stages.name: ordering
stages.brief: Place your order with the company above you (the factory starts production instead). The order reaches them next week.

ship.description: Ship beer to the company below you this week. You must clear your whole backlog before shipping anything else, and you can never ship more than your backlog plus the orders you have received.

when.why: You have nothing to ship.
You must clear your whole backlog before shipping anything else.
You do not have that much beer.
You cannot ship more than your backlog plus the orders you have received.

ship.outcome: You shipped {$got} cases to the company below you.

order.description: Order beer from the company above you (the factory starts production instead). The order reaches them next week.

amount.description: Cases to order from your supplier

order.outcome: You ordered {$params.amount} cases from your supplier.

events.name: customer demand
events.say: Customers order {$last($world.customer_demand)} cases of beer from the retailer this week.

position.title: Your position
position.show: It is week {$round} of {$inputs.weeks}. You are the {$actor.role}: stock {stock} cases, backlog {backlog} cases, orders waiting to be shipped {orders_in} cases, cost so far {$actor.cost|money}.

arrivals.title: This week
arrivals.show: Arrived: {last_received} cases. Shipped: {last_shipped} cases. Last order you placed: {last_order} cases.

pipeline.title: On the way to you
pipeline.show: {incoming} cases are on the way to you (production included, if you are the factory).

chain.title: Supply chain
chain.show: {role}: stock {stock}, backlog {backlog}, incoming {incoming}, orders_in {orders_in}, production {production}, cost {$it.cost|money}

customer_demand.description: Cases customers demanded each week, in week order

factory_orders.description: Cases the factory put into production each week, in week order

costs_by_role.description: Total cost of each company, by role

total_team_cost.description: Sum of all four companies' costs

bullwhip_ratio.description: Variance of the factory's weekly production orders divided by the variance of weekly customer demand

invariants.why: The supply chain has exactly four companies.
Stocks, backlogs and costs are never negative.
Beer is conserved: everything shipped or produced is in stock, in transit or delivered to customers.
